title: maniTC: a compiler for ManiT, a balanced-ternary systems programming language
description:
ManiT is a systems programming language in which balanced ternary is the native number system: integers are signed by construction, logic is three-valued (True / Unknown / False), and the fundamental control-flow construct is a three-way branch. maniTC is its compiler, written in Rust, with two backends.

The LLVM IR backend compiles and runs ManiT programs natively on ordinary binary hardware today, linking against an embedded C runtime. The T3ISA backend targets a balanced ternary instruction set, and ships with an assembler and a cycle-accurate emulator.

This is not a binary language with ternary features added. Balanced-ternary words and trytes, Kleene three-valued logic, three-way branching, balanced ternary floating point, and a ternary-native standard library are the foundation of the design rather than a layer over it.

Distributed under AGPL-3.0-or-later with the ManiT Runtime Library Exception covering the runtime and standard library, so programs compiled with maniTC are not themselves derivative works. A commercial licence is available.
